Chapter 7: The Power of Language and the Stories We Tell
Have you ever noticed how the words we use—sometimes without even thinking—can shape the world around us? It’s amazing how language doesn’t just describe reality; it actually helps create it. The way the media talks about events, the words institutions choose, even the stories we share with friends or tell ourselves at night... they all set the boundaries for what we believe is possible.
Imagine someone trying to talk about a tough moment in their life. Maybe it’s a loss, a big disappointment, or even a moment they’re ashamed of. The words they pick make all the difference. Calling that moment a “failure” feels a lot heavier than calling it a “lesson.” And saying, “I’m broken,” is nothing like saying, “I’m still learning.” The language we use becomes the lens through which we see ourselves, and even the world around us.
But it’s not just a personal thing. This holds true for whole cultures, too. The way we, as a society, talk about success, happiness, love, or justice actually shapes what we believe is possible. Take empowerment, for example. When advertising borrows empowering language for their own ends, it can twist the meaning of those words. Or think about politics—when debates get boiled down to catchy slogans or soundbites, we lose the depth and complexity of real issues.
Most of the time, we hardly notice how much language influences our reality. It’s like we’re fish, swimming in water we can’t see. But every once in a while, something happens—a new metaphor, a fresh way of telling a story—and suddenly, everything looks different. What once felt permanent or unchangeable? It turns out, that was just one way of seeing things.
Language holds real power. It can open our minds to new ideas, or it can shut us down. It can help us understand each other—or push us further apart. That’s why it’s so important to pay attention to the stories we’re telling—about ourselves, about other people, and about the world. Are those stories helping us grow, or are they holding us back?
Over time, you’ll see that the way we talk about things truly changes the way we experience them. The stories we repeat aren’t just echoes of what’s already happened; they’re tools for shaping what comes next. So, by choosing our words more thoughtfully, by exploring new ways of telling our stories, we can create more space for possibility—both for ourselves and for the world around us.
